canonical.title: Beginner → intermediate Obsidian: a roadmap for a developer with a 1,200-note vault

children.title: Properties & tagging for queryable notes
children.summary: Structured metadata so Bases and Dataview can query notes — when a property, when a tag, naming rules that keep both useful.

children.title: Bases: turn existing reference notes into live views
children.summary: .base format, conversion workflow, ready-to-steal recipes, formula language, and where Dataview still wins.

children.title: Linking & note structure: backlinks, MOCs vs folders
children.summary: Adoption-ordered path from folder-thinking to link-thinking: one wikilink per note, then three MOCs, then ACE/PARA only if needed.

children.title: Low-friction capture & daily-note habits
children.summary: Smallest viable capture loop — five-line daily-note template, one hotkey, one mobile pathway, one weekly pass — over four weeks.

children.title: Core + community plugins & keyboard-driven navigation
children.summary: Which core plugins to enable, the tight community-plugin starter pack, hotkey patterns that turn a beginner into keyboard-first.

sources.title: Obsidian Help — Bases
sources.claim: A .base file is empty until the notes it points at carry consistent YAML frontmatter.

sources.title: Practical PKM — Complete guide to properties
sources.claim: Add properties to templates; singular names, no spaces, lean on autocomplete; tag forward, never backfill.

sources.title: Practical PKM — Moving to Bases from Dataview
sources.claim: Bases ignores inline key::value Dataview metadata; YAML frontmatter only.

sources.title: Obsidian Help — Properties
sources.claim: Six property types (text, number, list, checkbox, date, date & time); singular tag/alias/cssclass deprecated 1.4, dropped 1.9.

sources.title: Obsidian Help — Link notes
sources.claim: Linking notes is the platform's core power; non-existent links appear muted as future seeds.

sources.title: MakeUseOf — Orphan notes & linking
sources.claim: One wikilink per new note before close, Graph View to spot orphans, 3 MOCs to absorb them, #needs-link batch.

sources.title: Aidan Helfant — 5 levels of MOCs
sources.claim: Five-level MOC adoption: isolated → linking → first MOC (Dump/Lump/Jump) → MOC-of-MOCs → Home note.

sources.title: Obsidian Rocks — How I use folders
sources.claim: Only 5 workflow folders (FINVA); folders force exclusivity that hurts as projects grow.

sources.title: Obsidian Rocks — Quick capture
sources.claim: The easier it is to create notes, the less likely you are to lose an important idea.

sources.title: Obsidian Help — Daily notes plugin
sources.claim: Daily Notes opens (or creates) a note based on today's date — journals, to-do lists, daily logs.

sources.title: GitHub — obsidian-periodic-notes
sources.claim: Periodic Notes extends the core daily-note idea to weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly.

sources.title: GitHub — Templater
sources.claim: Date math, JavaScript commands, folder-template triggers — needed for any daily template beyond static text.

sources.title: AIProductivity — Daily notes workflow
sources.claim: If your template has more than 10 sections you'll dread opening it; consistency > quality.

sources.title: Obsidian Help — Quick switcher
sources.claim: Ctrl/Cmd+O opens Quick Switcher; type to search, Enter to open, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter for new tab, Shift+Enter to create.

sources.title: XDA — Obsidian keyboard shortcuts
sources.claim: Four highest-leverage default hotkeys: Ctrl+P palette, Ctrl+O switcher, Ctrl+Shift+F global search, Ctrl+Shift+T reopen tab.

sources.title: Steph Ango — vault
sources.claim: Steph Ango (Obsidian CEO) uses ~4 folders; organises via links and properties; navigates with Quick Switcher and backlinks.

sources.title: Practical PKM — How to use tags effectively
sources.claim: Three-category taxonomy: type / status / topic. 'How will I search for this later' is the gate.

sources.title: DesktopCommander — tags in Obsidian
sources.claim: Frontmatter tags classify the whole note (status/type); inline tags mark content (#quote, #todo).

sources.title: Forum — MOC vs tagging
sources.claim: MOCs let you describe, order, and format what you link to; start with tags, add MOCs only when needed.

sources.title: Bagerbach — Weekly review
sources.claim: QuickAdd's author runs a Sunday weekly review aggregating project mentions; skipping days doesn't break the workflow.

sources.title: GitHub — Obsidian Git
sources.claim: Scheduled auto-commit-and-push, mobile-aware backup, Source Control view — standard free alternative to Obsidian Sync.

sources.title: GitHub — QuickAdd
sources.claim: QuickAdd combines templates, captures, macros, and multis behind single hotkeys.

sources.title: Obsidian Help — Core plugins
sources.claim: ~30 first-party core plugins ship with Obsidian; some disabled by default — Bases, Bookmarks, Canvas, Daily Notes, etc.

sources.title: Forum — Hotkey best practices
sources.claim: Prioritise left-hand-only chords for navigation; treat defaults as a starting point.

sources.title: dsebastien — Daily notes hub
sources.claim: Daily notes work best as the default hub; short-lived ideas get a default home.

sources.title: Obsidian Help — Tags
sources.claim: Tags must contain at least one non-numeric character; use / for nesting (#inbox/to-read); case-insensitive.

sources.title: GitHub — Dataview
sources.claim: Dataview still maintained but slowly; last release 0.5.70 (April 2025); no README sunset notice.
